title: punt init: handle upgrade of existing projects (scaffold vs. upgrade)
description:
punt init currently conflates two use cases: scaffolding new projects from scratch and upgrading existing projects to current standards. The scaffold case can be opinionated and overwrite freely. The upgrade case must be conservative — fill gaps without clobbering project-specific customizations.

CURRENT BEHAVIOR:
- _init_python_config: Conservative (checks before adding tool sections) — correct for upgrade
- _init_workflows: Compares content and overwrites if different — wrong for upgrade, steamrolls customizations like --all-extras, custom timeout-minutes, extra CI steps
- _init_claude_md: Conservative (checks for Standards References section) — correct for upgrade
- _init_beads: Conservative (checks if .beads/ exists) — correct for upgrade
- Missing entirely: markdownlint configs (.markdownlint.jsonc, .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc)

OBSERVED IN PRACTICE (langlearn-* projects):
Four new projects created by another agent have lint.yml/test.yml that are close to but intentionally different from punt-kit templates (use --all-extras, different timeout values). Running punt init would overwrite these with the generic template, losing valid customizations. Meanwhile, docs.yml and markdownlint configs are genuinely missing and should be added.

DESIGN QUESTION — DETERMINISTIC vs. LLM WORKFLOW:
An LLM-based upgrade workflow may be more appropriate than deterministic code because:
1. Upgrade requires judgment about what is a customization to preserve vs. drift to correct
2. The diff between existing and template is semantic, not just textual — an LLM can understand that --all-extras is intentional while a missing SHA pin is a gap
3. New standards evolve over time — an LLM can read current standards docs and apply them contextually rather than encoding rules in code
4. Projects have different valid reasons to diverge from templates (dependency groups, extra CI steps, platform-specific builds)

Possible approaches:
- A: punt init --upgrade flag (deterministic, only create missing files, never touch existing)
- B: punt init --diff (deterministic, show what would change, human decides)
- C: Jinja2 template variables (punt-kit-k79) that preserve customizations during re-render
- D: LLM workflow (Claude Code skill or agent) that reads standards, audits the project, and makes contextual decisions about what to fix — essentially punt audit --fix
- E: Hybrid — deterministic for truly mechanical files (markdownlint configs, docs.yml) + LLM for files that require judgment (lint.yml, test.yml, CLAUDE.md)

Option E (hybrid) may be the sweet spot: use deterministic code for files where the template IS the standard (no valid reason to diverge), and an LLM workflow for files where project-specific context matters.

title: Standard: --json global flag for CLI output
description:
All CLI tools should support a --json global flag for machine-readable output. This is a cross-cutting CLI standard that applies to biff, quarry, langlearn-tts, and future CLI projects.

## What
Add --json as a global typer option that switches all output to JSON. When enabled, commands emit structured JSON to stdout instead of human-formatted rich output. Errors also emit JSON to stderr.

## Why
Programmatic consumers (scripts, CI, other tools) need structured output. The current human-formatted output is unparseable. Every project has independently identified this need (biff-n68, quarry-imv, lltts-hx3).

## Standard definition needed
- Global flag: --json (typer callback or app-level option)
- Output contract: JSON to stdout, one object per command invocation
- Error contract: JSON to stderr with error field
- Document in standards/cli.md

## Adoption tracking (project beads)
- biff-n68: Add --json global flag to CLI
- quarry-imv: Add --json global flag to CLI
- lltts-hx3: Add --json global flag to CLI

title: Standard: PostToolUse output suppression hook for MCP plugins
description:
MCP server plugins in Claude Code should include a PostToolUse hook that suppresses verbose tool output from cluttering the conversation. This is a cross-cutting plugin integration pattern.

## What
A PostToolUse hook that intercepts MCP tool results and provides a concise summary instead of raw output. Prevents large search results, document contents, or verbose responses from consuming context window.

## Why
MCP tools often return large payloads (search results, document chunks, metadata). Without suppression, these dominate the conversation context. Both quarry and langlearn-tts have independently identified this need (quarry-uc2, lltts-5zg).

## Standard definition needed
- Hook type: PostToolUse prompt-based hook
- Pattern: match on tool name prefix, summarize output
- Document in standards/plugins.md

## Adoption tracking (project beads)
- quarry-uc2: Add PostToolUse output suppression hook
- lltts-5zg: Add PostToolUse output suppression hook

title: Add docs CI (markdownlint) to all repos missing it
description:
5 repos lack docs.yml workflow: biff, quarry, langlearn-tts, koch-trainer-swift, quarry-menubar.

Decisions:
- Exclude dot directories from linting: .claude/, .beads/, .venv/
- Exclude build artifacts: DerivedData/ (quarry-menubar)
- MD013: false (line length, org standard)
- MD060: false (table column style, org standard)
- MD024: false only in CHANGELOG.md files (duplicate headings are inherent to Keep a Changelog format). Use per-file markdownlint-disable comment, not global disable.
- MD033: allowed_elements=[img, p] (README layouts need width/align attributes)
- MD041: false for biff (plugin command files use frontmatter before h2)
- MD025: false for quarry (test fixtures have multiple h1)
- MD040: FIX (add language specifiers to fenced code blocks — real quality issue)
- MD032/MD022/MD031: FIX (blanks around lists/headings/fences — formatting)

Steps:
1. Create org-standard .markdownlint.jsonc template in punt-kit
2. Add .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc with ignorePatterns per repo
3. Fix remaining lint errors in each repo
4. Add docs.yml workflow (same as punt-kit template)
5. Update rulesets to require docs check
6. One PR per repo
close_reason: Added docs CI (markdownlint) to all 5 repos: biff#44, quarry#52, langlearn-tts#23, koch-trainer-swift#81, quarry-menubar#20. All merged. Updated rulesets to require docs check.

title: Standard: init subcommand for per-repo activation
description:
CLI tools that need per-repo configuration should provide an init subcommand that creates the necessary config files. This is a cross-cutting CLI pattern.

## What
An init subcommand (e.g. `quarry init`, `biff init`) that sets up per-repo configuration: creates config files, adds entries to .gitignore, and validates prerequisites. Idempotent — safe to run multiple times.

## Why
Tools like quarry and biff need per-repo activation (quarry needs a collection config, biff needs namespace config). Currently users must manually create these. Both projects have independently identified this need (quarry-pil, biff-80z).

## Standard definition needed
- Subcommand: `<tool> init`
- Behavior: create config files, update .gitignore, validate prerequisites
- Idempotent: safe to re-run, does not overwrite user customizations
- Output: report what was created/skipped
- Document in standards/cli.md

## Adoption tracking (project beads)
- quarry-pil: Add init subcommand for per-repo configuration
- biff-80z: Add init subcommand for per-repo activation
